minutes.headline: Task force leaned toward recommending a forensic accounting review and exploring CPA and a landfill lease; no formal votes.
minutes.summary: The Budget Task Force reviewed feedback from special town meeting, then went through its draft recommendation list: a landfill solar lease, Community Preservation Act adoption, payroll and purchase order efficiencies, merging school and town grounds work, preventive maintenance, health insurance, and a forensic accounting review. Members agreed to invite housing officials to the next flex meeting and to draft an executive summary. The only action taken was to pass over the prior minutes.

what_happened.line: The Budget Task Force took no formal votes; it only held the prior minutes over to its next meeting.
Members agreed a forensic accounting review should be the number one recommendation, with its scope capped.
A review of leasing the town dump site to a solar company was added to the recommendation list.
A split tax rate was set aside as explored but not viable, because a municipality cannot adopt one on its own.
The next flex meeting will focus on the Community Preservation Act and affordable housing; the chair will draft an executive summary.

why_it_matters: The list that results is a set of recommendations, not decisions, but a forensic accounting review, a Community Preservation Act adoption or a landfill lease could each reach residents as a town meeting vote or a change in how the tax levy is raised.
Health insurance claims were described as running above premium, with actual rates due in mid-January, which bears on what the town and schools must budget for employee coverage.
